ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that in $\triangle ABC$, with side $BC=6$ and height $AD=3$, the vertices $E$ and $F$ of the square $EFGH$ lie on side $BC$, while vertices $H$ and $G$ lie on sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. What is the length of the side of this square?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram:\\
$ \because $ Quadrilateral $EFMN$ is a square,\\
$ \therefore HG\parallel BC$, $HG=EF$,\\
$ \therefore \angle AHG=\angle B$,\\
$ \because \angle BAC=\angle BAC$,\\
$ \therefore \triangle AHG\sim \triangle ABC$,\\
$ \therefore \frac{AH}{AB}=\frac{HG}{BC}$,\\
Also $ \because AD\perp BC$,\\
$ \therefore AD\perp HG$, $HG=EF=MD$,\\
$ \because HG\parallel BC$,\\
$ \therefore \frac{AM}{AD}=\frac{AH}{AB}$, that is $\frac{AM}{AD}=\frac{HG}{BC}$,\\
Let $HG=x$, then $AM=AD-MD=3-x$,\\
$ \therefore \frac{3-x}{3}=\frac{x}{6}$, solving this gives: $x=\boxed{2}$,\\
$ \therefore $ The side length of this square is $2$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a large triangle ABC, with A at the top, and B and C at the two ends of the horizontal base BC. AD is the altitude from A perpendicular to the base BC, with foot D. Inside the triangle there is a square EFGH, with E and F on the base BC, H on side AB, and G on side AC; the upper side HG of the square is horizontal and parallel to the base BC. Reasoning: Let the side length of the square be x, then HG=EF=EH=FG=x. Because HG is parallel to BC, the small triangle AHG is similar to the large triangle ABC. The height of the large triangle from A to BC is AD=3. The height of the square upward from BC is x, so the distance from HG to BC is x, therefore the vertical distance from A to HG is 3-x. From the equality of the ratios of corresponding bases and corresponding heights in similar triangles, there is x/6 = (3-x)/3. Solve the equation: 3x = 6(3-x) = 18-6x, so 9x=18, obtaining x=2.
